Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with
complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with whiplash-type
cervical injury. The mechanism of injury is well matched to the reported symptoms.
Over the cuorse of care the patient attended 21 visits, which is somewhat longer than
typically expected for this type of injury, with treatment including manual therapy,
supervised therapeutic exercise, and home exercise instruction. Cervical range of
moiton was restricted on initial examination, with paraspinal muscle tenderness and
reduced strength noted. Imaging and clinical examination findings clearly confirm the
presence of soft tissue injury to the cervical spine. The patient reports no prior
injury or treatment involving the neck or upper back. Billing records reflect single
entries for each service rendered, with no duplicate or repeated charges identified.
Current status shows gardual improvement in pain and mobility, and the patient has
been discharged to a self-directed home program with follow-up as needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
